n: State Sponsorship and Commodity Trading Funding of Terrorism
ds: Terrorist organisations may receive support from state actors or raise revenue by controlling and trading commodities such as oil, minerals, antiquities and agricultural goods. Trade finance, front companies and commodity brokers can be used to convert resources into funds and move them to the group.

src.t: FATF, Financing of the Terrorist Organisation Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) (2015)
FATF, Financing of Recruitment for Terrorist Purposes (2018)
FATF, Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment Guidance (2019)

rat: Commodity trades (oil, minerals, antiquities) via brokers and front companies; state or quasi-state transfers to non-state actors; barter and cash settlement.

ind.n: Commodity trade originating from areas controlled by armed groups
ind.cx: Shipments of oil, minerals, scrap or agricultural goods with origin documentation tied to territory where terrorist groups operate.
ind.fp: Legitimate producers in border regions can have mixed supply chains.
ind.ds: Trade, production or payments involve territories controlled by armed groups or parties linked to them.
ind.cn: Armed-group territory or sanctioned parties in conflict areas

ind.n: Trading company with no operational history receives or sends commodity payments
ind.cx: Newly formed broker handles large commodity payments, has little physical presence and uses third-country accounts.
ind.ds: A recently formed customer with little history or track record quickly records large turnover or trades in high-value or restricted goods.
ind.cn: Newly established customer with rapid high-value activity

ind.n: Payments to intermediaries in neighbouring transit jurisdictions
ind.cx: Commodity proceeds are settled through agents or companies in jurisdictions adjacent to conflict areas and then forwarded onward.
ind.fp: Regional hubs are common commercial centres.
ind.ds: Commodity proceeds are settled through agents or companies in jurisdictions adjacent to conflict areas and then forwarded onward.

ind.n: Cultural property or antiquities sales with weak provenance
ind.cx: Trade in antiquities or artefacts with gaps in provenance linked to conflict-zone origin.
ind.fp: Older collections may have incomplete but benign provenance.
ind.ds: Trade in antiquities or artefacts with gaps in provenance linked to conflict-zone origin.

ind.n: Transactions involving entities tied to state support for designated groups
ind.cx: Counterparties publicly linked, by credible reports, to government support for terrorist organisations.
ind.fp: Government-owned entities are widely used in legitimate trade.
ind.ds: Counterparties publicly linked, by credible reports, to government support for terrorist organisations.

ind.n: Discrepancies between invoice, shipment and payment details
ind.cx: Quantity, price, consignee or route differs across documents in commodity transactions.
ind.fp: Errors and commercial renegotiation are routine.
ind.ds: Bill of lading, invoice, customs, letter of credit or payment details disagree on goods, quantity, price, origin, parties or route.
ind.cn: Trade documents inconsistent with each other

ind.n: Unusual use of cash or barter in commodity deals
ind.cx: Settlement via cash, barter or netting arrangements without documentation.
ind.fp: Barter and cash remain used in some commodity markets.
ind.ds: Settlement via cash, barter or netting arrangements without documentation.

ind.n: Funding flows following government transfers to non-state entities
ind.cx: Payments from state or quasi-state entities to private firms or individuals lacking evident services.
ind.fp: Grants and subsidies to private recipients are common.
ind.ds: Payments from state or quasi-state entities to private firms or individuals lacking evident services.

ctl.ds: Requires documentary evidence of origin, legal sourcing, custody and conformity with responsible-sourcing standards, including for informal or recycled supply. It keeps illicitly sourced goods from entering the financed or traded chain.

Compares shipping routes, ports and delivery points with typical lanes and risk lists, and requests explanation for unusual hubs or indirect delivery. It reveals diversion, transshipment and evasion routing.
Sets internal risk guidance, acceptance limits and approval levels for sectors, commodities and fundraising channels exposed to elevated risk. It gives consistent decisions on how far to engage.

Tests whether an entity has real operations such as premises, staff, stock and contracts through documents, site or virtual visits, open-source footprint and shell-risk indicators. It helps identify shell and front companies with no genuine activity.

ctl.n: Tightened monitoring for new accounts and entities
ctl.ds: Applies lower thresholds and closer review during the first months of an account or entity and alerts on turnover far above onboarding projections. It addresses the elevated risk at the start of a relationship.
Alerts when inflows are quickly moved out with little retained balance, including cash-in fast-out and rapid conversion or cash-out. It reveals accounts used as conduits for layering.
Risk-based vetting of intermediaries, brokers, partners and suppliers covering ownership, experience, references, public-official links and selection rationale. It limits exposure through proxies.

Briefs front-line, onboarding and investigation staff on current red flags, typologies and escalation routes, including sector-specific patterns and professional-enabler behaviours. It improves recognition of suspicious activity that rules alone cannot see.

Applies corroborated source-of-wealth checks, senior sign-off, enhanced monitoring and sceptical review of public-sector links for politically exposed persons and their networks. It targets the corruption and misappropriation risk specific to these customers.

ctl.n: PEP, relative and close associate screening
ctl.ds: Screens customers, beneficial owners, controllers, counterparties and their relatives and close associates against politically exposed person data at onboarding and on an ongoing basis. Matches trigger enhanced measures and senior approval.

Compares declared unit prices, award values, fees and ancillary costs with reference databases, estimates and comparable contracts, and requires documented rationale for outliers. It detects over- and under-invoicing and inflated awards.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.

Prohibits or caps cash for purchases, loans, donations and settlement above a set value, requiring documented non-cash methods and threshold reporting for dealers. It removes a low-traceability payment route.

Reconciles trade documents, invoices and shipments with the payments that settle them and reviews settlement made outside standard banking channels. It exposes trade-based laundering where payment logic does not match the underlying deal.

ctl.n: Public-funds payment monitoring and contract evidence
ctl.ds: Flags credits from public bodies to personal or new accounts, atypical state-to-private flows and onward movement, and requires contracts and tender evidence for payments from state entities. It targets diversion of public money.
